# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in five named phases, leveraging the fact that both systems can run concurrently (dual-run/parallel operation). The old system remains fully operational and untouched (no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning) until at least one full billing cycle after the final migration batch has been validated.

---

## Phase 0: Internal Validation ("Canary — Internal")

- **% of users:** 0% (0 real customers; internal/synthetic test accounts only, plus 5 opt-in employee accounts)
- **Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end QA in staging, including a full parallel-run reconciliation test against a snapshot of production billing data (invoice totals, tax calculations, and payment-method tokenization match legacy output within $0.01 on 100% of sampled test invoices), and rollback procedure has been dry-run successfully at least once.
- **Purpose:** Confirm dual-write/dual-read plumbing, data sync latency, and reconciliation tooling work correctly before any real customer is exposed.

## Phase 1: Early Adopters ("Pilot")

- **% of users:** 1% (~400 users), selected from low-complexity accounts (single currency, monthly billing, no active disputes, no enterprise contracts)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 0 exit metrics held for 5 consecutive business days with zero critical (Sev-1) defects, reconciliation mismatch rate = 0%, and support-ticket baseline established for comparison.
- **Purpose:** Validate real-world billing runs (charge, invoice, refund, dunning) on live but low-risk accounts, with both systems running in parallel and legacy remaining the system of record.

## Phase 2: Expansion ("Broad Rollout")

- **% of users:** 25% (~10,000 users), expanding to include mid-complexity accounts (multi-currency, annual billing, coupons/discounts) but still excluding top-tier enterprise accounts
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 1 ran for a minimum of one full billing cycle (≥30 days) with billing discrepancy rate < 0.1% of invoices, payment failure rate delta vs. legacy baseline ≤ 0.5 percentage points, and no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents open for more than 48 hours.
- **Purpose:** Stress-test the new system at meaningful scale across varied billing configurations while legacy continues running in shadow/parallel mode as a safety net.

## Phase 3: Majority Migration ("Scale-Up")

- **% of users:** 60% (~24,000 users), cumulative total 86% (~34,400 users), including most remaining segments except the highest-risk enterprise/custom-contract accounts
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained for ≥2 full billing cycles with reconciliation mismatch rate < 0.05%, customer-reported billing complaints not exceeding 1.2x the pre-migration baseline rate, and finance sign-off on revenue reporting parity between old and new systems.
- **Purpose:** Migrate the bulk of the user base once confidence is high, while still running both systems in parallel for cross-validation.

## Phase 4: Final Batch ("Long Tail Completion")

- **% of users:** 14% (~5,600 users) — the remaining users, including enterprise/custom-contract accounts requiring white-glove migration support
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 3 sustained for ≥1 full billing cycle with zero open Sev-1 incidents, reconciliation mismatch rate < 0.05%, and dedicated account managers have completed pre-migration outreach/scheduling with all remaining enterprise customers.
- **Purpose:** Complete migration of the final and most complex accounts. **Note:** Per requirement, the legacy system is NOT deleted, disabled, or decommissioned during this phase — it remains live in read-only/fallback mode.

## Phase 5: Legacy Decommissioning (Post-Migration — Separate Phase)

- **% of users:** N/A (no user migration activity; all 40,000 users are already on the new system)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 4 has been complete for ≥1 full billing cycle (≥30 days) with zero critical billing discrepancies, all historical data has been archived and verified, finance and compliance have signed off, and a final audit confirms 100% of invoices for the most recent cycle were generated correctly by the new system alone.
- **Purpose:** Only now is the legacy system placed into cold storage/archival and formally decommissioned — deliberately separated from Phase 4 so decommissioning never overlaps with the final migration batch.

---

## Rollback Strategy

At every phase, users can be reverted to the legacy system as the system of record by flipping a per-account routing flag, since both systems run in parallel and legacy continues processing in shadow mode until Phase 5. Rollback of a batch must complete within 4 hours of a halt decision.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

The rollout is automatically halted (no further users migrated, and rollback of the current phase's batch is considered) if any of the following occur:

- **Reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 0.5%** of invoices in any 24-hour window (comparing new-system output to legacy shadow calculation).
- **Payment failure rate** in the new system exceeds the legacy baseline by more than **2 percentage points** over any rolling 24-hour period.
- **Sev-1 incident count** related to billing exceeds **2 in a single week**, or any single Sev-1 remains unresolved for more than **8 hours**.
- Customer support ticket volume tagged "billing issue" for migrated cohorts exceeds **3x** the pre-migration per-user baseline rate over a 7-day window.

---

## Risks

RISK: Double-charging or missed charges due to dual-system race conditions during the parallel-run window | Implement idempotency keys and a single authoritative charge-orchestrator that locks each account to one active billing engine at a time | Engineering Lead, Billing Platform

RISK: Data drift between old and new systems causing reconciliation reports to become unreliable over time | Run automated hourly reconciliation jobs with alerting on mismatch thresholds, and require manual sign-off before advancing any phase | Data Engineering Lead

RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing invoicing disputes and revenue loss | Defer all enterprise/custom-contract accounts to the final phase with dedicated account-manager review and manual QA of each contract mapping | VP Finance Operations

RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a phase, delaying detection of a systemic issue | Pre-train support staff on new-system troubleshooting and staff up before each phase start based on cohort size | Head of Customer Support

RISK: Rollback of a migrated batch fails or is slower than expected, extending customer impact | Require a tested, automated rollback script per phase and conduct a rollback drill before that phase begins | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 5
